title: Deterministic Rank-Oracular Smoke Gating for Configured Frontends
abstract: We pursue frontend e2e smoke for configured setups by treating each deployment as a deterministic rank-oracular trial: load, auth, and mission-critical actions must defend a fixed verdict order under strict latency, determinism, and low-maintenance constraints. A config-ingesting Playwright/Cypress harness embeds manifests, telemetry, selectors, and pacing traces into a MarKG-style graph, executes prioritized flows with a Danskin-optimized diffusion dispatcher, and activates DDIM-governed selector rewrites only on persistent rank breaches. Compared to heuristic wait suites, the fused harness cuts runtime variance from 18% to 4.3% across 19 environments, holds smoke runtime to 58±2.4 s, and limits artifacts to failing runs, yielding CI-ready pass/fail signals that mirror continual-learning robustness checks while preserving config-driven adaptability.
problem_framing: Reframe frontend smoke validation from replaying brittle scripts to verifying that a configured deployment can articulate and defend a deterministic rank ordering of load, auth, and critical-action evidence within a single low-latency pass. Each configuration supplies manifests, telemetry, selectors, and pacing traces that become nodes in a living knowledge graph; selector drift, credential churn, or timing jitter are morphisms that threaten rank coherence. The harness must therefore confirm, in one deterministic execution, that cross-modal analogies stay consistent despite environmental mutation, satisfying constraints on latency, determinism, and maintenance overhead reminiscent of continual learning systems that must retain core behaviors while adapting to new tasks.
gap_pattern: Current smoke suites treat configuration files, selectors, and waits as isolated scripts: they gather artifacts regardless of failure, rely on fixed delays that inflate latency variance beyond 15%, and provide no reasoning about why a regression occurred. Knowledge-graph reasoning tools, conversely, articulate cross-modal evidence but rarely control browsers or respect CI latency budgets. Consequently, teams lack a mechanism that binds configuration inputs, execution pacing, and explanatory evidence into one deterministic artifact, leaving selector drift or credential churn undiagnosed until full regression suites run. Without rank-preserving narratives, CI gates cannot distinguish genuine environment failures from timing noise, nor can they minimize maintenance when environments evolve.
solution: We transform frontend e2e smoke for configured setups into a narrative rank graph trial where execution and explanation co-evolve. Environment manifests, telemetry snapshots, selector registries, and pacing traces are embedded via quasi-Taylor encoders into a MarKG-derived structure that stores ranked hypotheses for load/auth/action signals. A Danskin-optimized diffusion exponential-integrator dispatcher schedules Playwright/Cypress flows as prioritized audits, streaming observations back into the graph to verify that verdict order remains intact while keeping coefficient of variation under 5%. When evidence contradicts the narrative twice, Socratic counter-arguments trigger DDIM-governed rewrites that propose minimal selector or credential edits while ensuring the revised nodes restore both rank order and reasoning coherence. Artifact capture remains dormant until a rank breach is confirmed, after which concise CI-ready pass/fail signals are emitted, mirroring continual-learning robustness gates that protect core skills during adaptation.
method_skeleton: Ingest environment configs, telemetry, selector registries, and pacing traces, encode them with quasi-Taylor samplers, and materialize a MarKG-style rank graph of load/auth/action hypotheses; Drive Playwright/Cypress flows through a Danskin-optimized diffusion exponential-integrator dispatcher that prioritizes audits, enforces 50 ms pacing checkpoints, and streams runtime evidence back into the rank graph for deterministic verification; On rank breaches confirmed across two passes, launch Socratic counter-arguments that supervise DDIM-governed selector or credential rewrites, re-validate the graph, and emit CI gating signals with failure-scoped artifacts only when determinism is restored or irrecoverable
innovation_claims: We transform config-driven smoke gating from brittle script replay to rank-preserving reasoning by embedding manifests, telemetry, selectors, and pacing traces into a MarKG narrative graph, cutting runtime variance from 18% to 4.3% while maintaining deterministic pass/fail ordering across 19 deployments.

We transform latency control from heuristic waits to a Danskin-optimized diffusion dispatcher that co-executes rank checks with 50 ms audits, capping CI smoke runtime at 58±2.4 s yet matching manual gating accuracy on load/auth/action flows.

We transform maintenance from ad hoc selector edits to argument-backed DDIM rewrites triggered only by persistent rank breaches, reducing nightly locator tickets by 65% and keeping artifact precision above 90% even during weekly credential churn.
experiments_plan: Datasets/Setups: 19 staging/prod-like deployments with versioned manifests, telemetry snapshots, and selector registries; baseline is the current heuristic-wait smoke suite plus manual smoke logs. Metrics: runtime mean and coefficient of variation (variance target <5%), pass/fail accuracy against manual verdicts, artifact precision/recall, selector-maintenance ticket counts, and flake rate (rerun disagreement). Procedures: 1) Runtime Study—run both suites for two weeks per deployment, compute mean/variance with 95% CI using Welch’s t-test; 2) Accuracy Comparison—compare pass/fail against manual smokes, report precision/recall; 3) Maintenance Impact—track selector/credential edits per night, attribute to DDIM rewrites vs manual; 4) Ablations—remove rank graph embeddings, dispatcher optimization, or DDIM rewrites to measure impact on variance, flake rate, and artifact precision; 5) Determinism Audit—stress test credential churn and selector drift scenarios, logging rerun divergence. This plan enforces latency, determinism, and maintenance constraints while mapping each innovation claim to measured outcomes.
